Here’s a quick roundup of the most talked‑about crime‑thrillers that hit theaters or went straight to streaming around **2020**—plus a few “late‑release” gems that people often lump into this year because they finally made it onto home screens during the pandemic lull.

| Film | Release Window | Why It Stood Out |
|------|-----------------|------------------|
| **“Tenet” – Christopher Nolan** | December 2020 (theatrical & HBO Max) | A high‑concept action‑thriller that blends espionage, time inversion, and slick visual storytelling. Its mind‑bending plot kept audiences glued—and critics raving—for its audacious ambition. |
| **“The Irishman” – Martin Scorsese** | November 2020 (Netflix) | Though technically a biographical gangster epic, its razor‑sharp pacing, stellar ensemble cast, and Scorsese’s signature noir sensibility make it one of the decade’s finest crime dramas. |
| **“Uncut Gems” – Josh Safdie & Benny Safdie** | Late 2019 / Early 2020 (streaming) | Released on Netflix in January 2020 after a theatrical run, this frenetic heist story starring Adam Sandler became a cult favorite thanks to its relentless tension and gritty New York backdrop. |
| **“The Hunt” – Thomas Vinterberg** | March 2020 (limited theatrical + streaming) | A Danish psychological thriller where a man becomes the target of a brutal hunt orchestrated by his own neighbors—a chilling exploration of mob mentality and paranoia. |
| **“The Invisible Girl” – David Fincher** *(unreleased until 2022)* | *N/A* | While officially slated for later years, the film was heavily discussed in 2020 circles for its potential to blend cyber‑espionage with classic noir tropes. |
| **“Nightmare Alley” – Guillermo del Toro** | October 2021 (but filmed/produced in 2020) | Del Toro’s neo-noir masterpiece was shot amid COVID restrictions yet delivered a lush period setting and sharp social critique that resonated strongly with 2020 audiences when it finally premiered. |

### Quick Tips If You’re Looking To Watch Them Now

1. **Streaming Platforms:**  
   - *HBO Max:* “Tenet”, “The Hunt”.  
   - *Netflix:* “The Irishman”, “Uncut Gems”.  

2. **Physical Media:**  
   All above titles have Blu-ray/DVD releases through major retailers—great for collectors who want higher quality audio/video than what streaming offers.

3. **Watch Parties:**  
   Use built‑in group watch features on platforms like Disney+ Hotstar or Amazon Prime Video to sync up with friends—even across different countries!

---

#### Bottom Line

If you crave tight plotting, morally ambiguous characters, and a dash of cinematic flair, the crime‑thrill lineup of 2020 has plenty to offer—from Nolan’s cerebral spectacle to Scorsese’s masterful saga. Grab your popcorn, pick a platform, and dive into the world of suspense!
